#1503. Jurgen Klopp reveals he confronted Germany star over controversial crown celebration with links to 'anti-LGBTQ+ group' - and promises he won't repeat it

Published: 12:42 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 15:09 EST, 13 November 2026

Germany manager Jurgen Klopp insists midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a controversial goal celebration after opposition from supporters.

Nmecha, a Christian player for Borussia Dortmund, was criticised last weekend for celebrating scoring by lowering an imaginary crown from his head onto the pitch.

The celebration - called 'The King's Return' - was popularised by an evangelical network of footballers called Ballers in God, which counts prominent Premier League players among its members. It is supposed to represent the idea of submission to God.

But an investigation by German outlets found that the campaign website for 'The King's Return' linked to a chat service run by an organisation called Groundwire, where counsellors shared anti-homosexual views and described abortion as 'Satan's Plan'. Daily Mail Sport encountered similar views when consulting the service.

Nmecha has maintained that his message was one of love, but after a huge outcry in Germany - and talks with Klopp and national team sporting director Rudi Voller - he will not adopt the celebration again.

Klopp said: 'It was a big ⁠issue. I saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time. But then it all kicked off.

Felix Nmecha has vowed not to repeat his 'King's Return' celebration after a huge outcry

He was called into a meeting with Jurgen Klopp and Germany's sporting director Rudi Voller for the celebration which is connected with evangelical Christian group Ballers in God

'As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

'I have known Felix Nmecha for a few months, and I can say that he is a very friendly young man, who is warm and open, and always spreads positive energy when he is with us.

'I confronted him with all the things you might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone.

'For me ⁠the most important issue was settled. Then I said "how do we do it with the goal ⁠celebration?" He will not be celebrating like that.'

A vocal section of Dortmund fans opposed the club signing Nmecha from Wolfsburg in 2023 after he had shared anti-homosexual and anti-transgender posts.

Ballers in God was founded in 2015 by former Tottenham midfielder John Bostock and brings together a wide range of Christian players from across the pyramid with weekly sessions.

While the organisation does not hold an explicit stance on LGBTQ+ issues, their Instagram account did celebrate the end of the Rainbow Laces campaign in the Premier League last year.

In response to the Nmecha story, they wrote: 'We are encouraged by player-led movements such as The King's Return, where footballers themselves take the initiative to express their faith in Jesus.

Klopp says Nmecha told him he 'loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone'

'Our desire is not only to share our hope, but to demonstrate love and respect towards everyone, including those who do not share our beliefs.

'Our focus has always been, and will always be, to point people to Jesus with grace and love.'

Nmecha said: 'My message has never been about promoting intolerance, discrimination, or hate in any form.'

Back at Dortmund, Nmecha, 26, still faces scrutiny. A supporters' group claimed that his celebration clashed with club values and he has been reprimanded by senior figures.

The club's president, Hans-Joachim Watzke, said: 'The fan department has every right to start a discussion like this. I was at their annual general meeting on Monday. It was clear that those who were bothered by parts of his celebration were in a significant majority. So you have to take it seriously and discuss it.

'If he scores a goal and points his index fingers upwards, everyone knows he wants to thank God. He is also welcome to make the sign of the cross.

'But placing the crown on the grass - that is, of course, somewhat linked to Ballers in God. I don’t even want to judge it. When I look at what they stand for, Borussia Dortmund’s code of core values and Ballers in God’s fundamental outlook are not entirely compatible. We don’t want that in our living room.

'I told him: "Felix, if you sense that it is dividing the fans, perhaps you will also realise that you shouldn’t do it any more." He wants to think about it. We had a wonderful conversation with him. We had a one-hour video call. That is where we are now, and he will think about it. I hope we can find a sensible solution.

'I like Felix Nmecha very much. We have a very, very good relationship and speak frequently. As a practising Catholic, I am the last person who would want to forbid someone from praying. That is not what this is about at all. It is legitimate, too. The only question we are discussing with him is the second part of his celebration.'

#1502. Roma monitoring Germany starlet Derry Scherhant

Derry Scherhant, born in 2002 and owned by Freiburg, is winning over Germany coach Jurgen Klopp.

In the 5-0 win over Malen’s Netherlands, Scherhant started and scored the opening goal.

A great long-range goal and a brilliant performance. Scherhant is a right-footed attacking winger who arrived at Freiburg in the summer of 2025 for just €2 million from Hertha Berlin.

A real bargain, considering his value has now significantly increased.

As reported by calciomercato.com, Roma have long been interested in Scherhant.

Ahead of the winter transfer window, the Giallorossi are looking for a right-footed left winger with the same characteristics as the German: built (185 cm), speed, and finishing ability. This season with Freiburg, he scored two goals and four assists in nine Bundesliga appearances.

#1501. Lethal Trent Alexander-Arnold sends Tuchel a statement in England victory

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24

Will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the big delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon said of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”

A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

As for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

“Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel said. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL

England had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

“I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold said later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”

Kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

“If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel said when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against New Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

“But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

Trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

“He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel said.

“He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. He scored against Spain, so he has decisive actions and he’s defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he’s a very important player.”

England returned to winning ways with a 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague.

Pavel Sulc’s first-half red card after a VAR review of his clumsy challenge on Elliot Anderson took the sting out of the initially lively hosts and Anthony Gordon gave Thomas Tuchel’s men a deserved lead early in the second half.

The forward headed home a fantastic cross by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start under the German coach, before skipper Harry Kane scored to settle any nerves.

So who played well for England and who failed to impress? Rate each player with our voting tool, and have your say in the comments.

I thought we were very professional second half. We stepped up and needed to be more dynamic, bring more urgency into our play, which we did. We kept that intensity going and and the effort was till there. Deserved victory.

Strange to get an early red card. Not the best for the spectators, not the best for the team. It’s an awkward one. But we got the win.

To guide it into the goal, there was an awful lot [for Anthony Gordon] to do. Good pass, good goal. Both full-backs were good. The position in the second half suited Trent more than the position in the first half. Lewis was excellent on the other side.

We have used all the outfield players after two matches so credit to all of them. Now it’s important to relax and enjoy the evening, do a good recovery and prepare for Saturday.

I think it was good. They go down to 10 men and it should be easier for us to win the game, But in fact it makes it more difficult. They get very compact and defend with a lot of players around the box and it’s hard to break them down.

We got that [goal] at the start of the second half which is what we needed. The longer it’s 0-0, it gets harder and harder and harder.

[Where do you place your assist?]  It’s up there for sure. I spoke to Ant at half-time and said if I get into those half-spaces I’m looking to put it in so make sure you get to the back post. I didn’t expect it to work so quickly.

He’s a willing runner, great to play with him. I saw the run and was able to execute the pass,

It’s always a pleasure and an honour to represent my country. It’s been a long time. I’ve always believed that I can play for England and I want to. The manager’s given me the opportunity and I tried to do what he wanted me to do to the best of my ability and I hope he’s happy with how I played.

🦁 #1301Alex Scott reflects on a special night, earning his first senior England cap 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/lC34bAPbbd

It was good, quite dominant. We created a lot of chances but without the quality. When they went a man down, we were too passive at times. We need to be dominant, as I said earlier, go for the throat and put teams away.

I said that to him [Trent, on the quality of the ‘assist’]. I make that run time and time again but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry, he would have loved to have played more.

I’ve missed playing with Hally. He’s a good lad. We had great chemistry at Newcastle and it’s great to share this stage with him.

It’s my only header. I’d be the worst header of the ball you’ll ever see. Really happy, resally proud to score that because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.

Perfectly competent and signs of promise in the left-back/left-wing axis. England looked too open against 11 men and better teams – hola España – may have capitalised on the sloppiness. But once Sulc was sent off, England gradually turned the screw and created a hatful of chances, running out easy winners.

Another tidy save from Kovar when Bellingham receives a pass from the left, strides towards the D, then drives a daisy-cutter towards the left of goal. The keeper swoops down early to turn it behind with a stiff wrist.

Two minutes of stoppage time are signalled as England try to pen the home side in their own half.

Tuchel has kept the back four on the pitch for the 90 minutes. He was not entirely happy with them in the first half – or his body language suggested that, anyway. But it is a welcomed clean sheet for England after the chaotic defeats to Spain and France.

Ngumoha is enjoying himself and showing off some excellent close control.

Scott and Eze smash shots over the bar from 22 yards within a minute of each other.

Rogers’ diagonal cross is chested down by Eze as he sets up an opportunity to shoot in the area but a defender hacks it away. Ngumoha pounces on the loose ball and plays a neat reverse pass with the outside of his boot to Rogers on the underlap. Rogers goes for power rather than lift to find Eze or Bellingham and the keeper makes another smart save.

Gibbs-White’s pace and direct running have the beating of Chaloupek and he tees up Eze to hammer a left-foot shot that seemed to be arrowing into the net until Kovar stuck up his right hand to paw it over.

Gordon stops, then from a standing start drives past bursts past Chaloupek to the byline and stands up a near-post cross that Rogers flashes wide.

Czech Republic break after England’s attack down the right hits the skids. Hlozek gallops down the middle and lets fly before Scott can catch him. Trafford sees it all the way, dives to his right to save and gathers the loopy effort from the rebound.

Slama hounds Ngumoha into conceding a corner as the Liverpool winger slips under pressure.

Jude Bellingham is wearing the England captain’s armband again. He was also wearing it during the pre-World Cup camp against New Zealand. Thomas Tuchel explained afterwards that the player with the most caps is skipper when Harry Kane is subbed off. Bellingham is also playing centrally, as a False Nine.

Bellingham → KaneNgumoha → SakaScott → Anderson.

England have switched to the Revie Plan with Bellingham as the deep-lying centre-forward.

Czech Republic 0 England 2 (Kane) Eze plays Rogers in down the left of the box. He gets there but falls under the tackle of Krejci, knocking the ball to Kane who thumps it through Hranac’s legs with his left foot from about seven yards.

KANE DOUBLES ENGLAND'S LEAD 🔥Harry Kane in the right place at the right time for the Three Lions 🦁#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/Od9x5kXOsH

Kane stuck around five finishes into that corner in the warm-up. Same finish - accurate and powerful. Finally a first cap for Alex Scott.

As Sam Matterface points out. England having a left-footed left-back has added an extra dimension to their attacking play. I never thought I’d be quoting Sam Matterface but it’s been one of those days. Ambros had taken up a good position in space on the left but the crossfield pass wasn’t good enough and sailed beyond him.

Alexander-Arnold shoots from the right after some slow-slow-slow-quick passing between him and Saka opens up a gap. But he drills it across goal and wide of the left post.

Now Hall does find the target at his third attempt this half but only because Krejci is there to deflect his cross on to the post with the keeper beaten.

Corner on the right for England who procrastinate so long over their positions the referee warns them but does not take it off them. Krejci and Kane have their arms around each other as the ball comes in and the Czech captain pulls Kane to the ground but the referee waves play on.

Saka takes it short and plays a one-two with Alexander-Arnold. Saka cuts it back to Eze to shoot in a pre-cooked move but he is closed down too quickly so he rolls it to Hall 20 yards out and the left-black leans back and launches his shot 20 rows back behind the goal.

England have a corner on the left after a last gasp tackle by Chaloupek on Gordon.

Czech Republic have switched to 3-3-3 in possession and are trying to play. Sadilek is struggling after being kicked by person or persons unknown. Apologies.

Although the goal was built from the right, England have been so dominant down the left. Hall and Gordon, who combined so well for Newcastle, do so again here with the left-back creeping up the inside while the winger goes down the outside and plays it into the box for his former colleague who wafts his shot wide with a lazy air from 15 yards. Should have scored.

Czech Republic 0 England 1 (Gordon) Alexander-Arnold clears Lingr’s cross and runs upfield to join the counter that seems to break down. But a crossfield pass from the home side is picked off by the right-back facing his own goal 30 yards from the Czechs’. He turns and arrows a fine cross to the left of the penalty spot. Gordon lets it bounce and cushions a header back across the keeper and in at the right post. Great finish. High IQ finish as he might say.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3️⃣ goals in his last 4️⃣ games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/iej0PCW8Ar

That goal was all about Trent. He intercepted in his own penalty area before making a 70-run up the pitch to get on the end of a throughball. That doesn’t work but he wins the ball back and crosses for Gordon to score. The full house from Trent there – showing Tuchel what he brings to the team in just a few seconds of action.

England are attcking from right to left in the second half. England’s trumpeter is in the house and reprises the national anthem.

Eze → Lewis-Skelly who was on a yellow card.

Just before half-time, Krejci, the Wolves centre-half wiped out Saka, watching the man, not the ball, and bodychecking him.

Thomas Tuchel was furious with the fourth official Cihan Aydin, wagging his finger in anger after Bukayo Saka was taken out by Ladislav Krejci. Before that he was quite passive on the touchline, hands in pockets as he watched England trying to break down the Czechs.

Could be another tactical half-time substitution for Myles Lewis-Skelly. Czech players definitely see him as the best chance of a red for England.

The Czech Republic were causing England problems with 11 men but having been reduced to 10 have concentrated on trying to persuade the referee to even up the numbers and also on defending in a low block. Gordon and Hall have the key to unlock the defence but too often when they have sent crosses in, Kane has been in wild rover mode.

Kane takes the ball by the left of the D, spins to wrap his right instep around the ball and try to bend it into the top right corner. Kovar, the PSV goalkeeper, soars to his left to claw it away with his top hand.

Kovář DENIS Harry Kane! 🛑England pushing for a goal before half time 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/l4lAeAl6IE

Karabec is not going to be able to continue. Good cross from Hall from the left wins the applause of Kane. So near.

Karabec is hurt in a collision with Alexander-Arnold that the referee does not deem a foul.

Every tackle, every collision inspires a Czech demand for a red card. Karabec hits the deck like a bag of hammers when brushed by Rogers’ arm but the referee isn’t buying the implication that he had been elbowed.

Lewis-Skelly ignores Hall’s underlapping run down the inside left and pops it short to Guehi instead. The City defender slips a pass down the outside for Gordon who dribbles into the box and clips an inviting, low cross through the six-yard box. Rogers may have got a touch at the near post and the ball runs across goal. Karabec juts about gets it away,  avoiding the risk of shanking it into his own goal.

Krejci wants a tot-for-tat red card for Lewis-Skelly who slid in and caught Cerv on the foot. He never raised his studs and yellow suffices. The manager Santi is also booked for protesting the colour.

The system seems to be working again. Apologies for the break in updates.

Good work by Kane down the left to get away from Chaloupek and run into the box. He clips a short pass to the near post that Saka tries to finish, improvising a flick, that balloons wide off a defender. The angle made that all but impossible.

That is a big moment in the game, with Pavel Sulc dismissed for a stamp on Elliot Anderson. There was little protest about the foul when it occurred. In fact, even a yellow was a bit surprising. But Umut Meler was sent to the pitchside monitor. Czech Republic looked lively but you would now expect them to sit back and defend.

Czechs are now in a 5-4-0 formation. This will be a test of England to break through the two lines of defence. It will be like the Ghana match at the World Cup.

Pavel Sulc, who was playing so well, has been sent off after the referee was sent to the monitor by VAR. It was a high tackle, catching Anderson’scalf with his studs.

Czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL

That red card has deprived the Czech Republic of their best player so far. He took it well rather than going off in a Sulc.

Big test for Czech manager Santi Denia, once of Atlético Madrid, who was manager of Spain U17s when they lost the 2017 final to an England team featuring – among other luminaries – Marc Guéhi and Morgan Gibbs-White.

Gordon cuts in from the left on to his right and flashes a shot across goal that flies past the right post.

SO CLOSE FROM GORDON!🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/MUiKO8TqvC

Apologies we have been having some technical issues.

England had their best chance in the 16th minute when Rogers spun by the penalty spot. He was facing Anthony Gordon to collect his pass in from the left. Pirouetting, he steadies himself to thump a left-foot shot into the foot of the right post. The ball rebounds to Anderson who flays a shot from 18 yards that Chaloupek throws himself in front of to block only to divert it to Saka and Hranac is there to block that one.

How have England not scored!? 🤯Somehow Czech Republic keep the score at 0-0 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 🇨🇿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/51tmBwgRRf

England are dicing with danger in not picking up Sulc.

What was Thomas Tuchel saying about his England players being a danger to themselves around the box? It was an error there from Elliot Anderson that let Czech Republic through on goal and a better touch from Pavel Sulc would have seen them take the lead. Harry Kane dropped deep to start England’s attack down the right. The flanks will be their route to goal in this game.

Alexander-Arnold loses the ball in the middle of the park. Radosta is sent down the right by a cute pass and he gulls Hall by crossing early after shaping to go down the line. Alexander-Arnold is back to head it away but only as far as Cerv who torpedoes a volley from 25 yards barely a foot wide of the right post.

Kane is given a talking to for tangling with the Czech captain Krejci, giving him a deserved shove hopefully for the heinous crime of wearing the No 7 shirt while playing at centre-half.

Lewis-Skelly mops up at the back after a third rapid Czech Republic break, this one down the right with Chaloupek to the fore. Shielding the ball in the penalty area, he buys a foul and England build again from a free-kick.

Lovely pass by Rogers sends Saka down the right and the Arsenal winger tries to whip over a cross to pick up Kane’s near-post dart but it goes behind the England captain.

Mistake by Anderson lets Lyon’s Sulc pounce on to possession and dribble down the inside-left, cutting into the centre of the field as he approaches the box with Chalobah in pursuit. The ball skids off the greasy turf as he gets closer to the 18-yard line and Trafford sprints and slides to get there first.

Chaloupek is stalking Gordon all over the pitch and Slama is sticking close to Saka. First decent move down the Czech right catches Guehi a little off guard but out comes Trafford to gather.

No clean sheets for England in six games since the victory over Panama in the last group game in the United States and they have made three changes in the back four.

You can read an obituary of the former West Ham goalkeeper here.

Every fan, player, coach and journalist on their feet for the tribute to Luděk Mikloško, who passed away earlier this month.

We had a chat this morning. Both our hearts said 60 minutes, but both our heads said 30 minutes make more sense.

Time for the national anthems. God Save the King followed by Kde domov muj. England are in all white, the home side in red shirts, navy shorts and socks (or, as the old Rothmans’ annuals used to put it, ‘hose’).

Thomas Tuchel’s name was read out by the stadium announcer here at Fortuna Arena – unlike at Wembley last weekend. There was no way to gauge the fans’ view of Tuchel before the win over Spain as he was not mentioned and his image was not on the big screens. Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

Santi started his stint in charge and this campaign in Group A3 with a 2-1 defeat by Croatia but there were some very positive signs – they set up as a 4-3-3 in classic Spanish/Cruyff style and pressed like dervishes. England, who conceded three goals when players made mistakes when subjected to aggressive pressing in their opening 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain, will have to find better solutions tonight, either by holding their nerve or counterpressing with fewer mistakes.

Given England are ranked 45 places higher, their results, if not all performances, at the World Cup were commendable and the way in which they rattled Spain and should really have given themselves a bulwark against the comeback by converting their penalty at 2-1 up,  an away win should be relatively straightforward. But they did lose on their last visit to Prague in a Euro 2020 qualifier having won 5-0 in the home leg.

#1500. Roma and Lazio interested in Federico Chiesa for January

Federico Chiesa’s future could bring him back to Italy after a stint at Liverpool that fell far short of expectations.

In three seasons with the Reds, the attacking winger has failed to regain the consistency and performance that made him a star with Fiorentina, Juventus, and the national team.

This situation, on the cusp of turning thirty, could push him to seek a new opportunity to relaunch his career. The most likely option would be a loan deal on advantageous terms, a solution that would satisfy both Liverpool and the player.

The English club would have the opportunity to develop Chiesa, potentially increasing his attractiveness on the transfer market, while the striker could return to playing more regularly. Also in the background is his goal of joining the national team, which he has been absent from for over two years.

With Roberto Mancini as manager, a return to the Italian league could offer him a chance to reclaim the Azzurri jersey, provided he can demonstrate on the pitch that he has regained his peak condition.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, the most interesting prospects for the former Juventus player’s future lie in Rome, where both clubs in the capital could be evaluating his potential arrival. On the Giallorossi front, Gian Piero Gasperini is seeking additional attacking options and would be interested in adding a player with Chiesa’s qualities, especially in a low-cost move. Much will depend, however, on the financial terms of the potential transfer and the player’s fitness.

Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio could also enter the race, considering the possibility of strengthening their attack with an experienced player. The competition between the two Roman clubs does not, however, rule out interest from other Italian clubs, especially if Liverpool decides to facilitate the winger’s departure.

#1498. Gasperini eyes Ruben van Bommel as Roma’s top target

Roma is looking to the Netherlands to find the attacking winger requested by Gian Piero Gasperini.

At the top of the list of possible reinforcements is Ruben van Bommel, the 22-year-old striker for PSV Eindhoven and the Dutch national team. Journalist Piero Torri revealed the news this morning on Manà Manà Sport Roma.

The son of a talented player, he’s one of the players the Giallorossi are most confidently targeting to strengthen their attack.

Van Bommel perfectly fits the profile of the winger Gasperini is seeking: he plays primarily on the left flank, is right-footed, has an imposing build, stands nearly 1.90 meters tall, and combines speed, power, and the ability to beat his opponent. He loves to start wide and then cut inside to shoot, but he’s also capable of attacking deep.

He’s a player with particularly interesting characteristics for the Roma coach’s aggressive, vertical style of football.

Van Bommel is being supported by Team Raiola and has a contract with PSV until June 2030. The Dutch club invested around €16 million to acquire him from AZ and would be unlikely to let him leave on particularly favorable terms. This is an aspect that Roma will eventually have to evaluate, along with the deal’s formula and the financial margins for January’s move.

#1497. Personal incentives for public officials drove a drop in China’s fertility

Jia Yu is at the Center for Social Research, Guanghua School of Management, Peking University, Beijing 100871, China.

China’s one-child policy is probably the best-known population-control programme in history, yet in its first decade it barely changed the country’s fertility rate. Writing in Nature, Meng et al.1 show that the biggest drop in fertility after the policy’s introduction was driven by a change in how officials were incentivized to enforce it. This change accounts for about half of the fall in the country’s fertility rate during the 1990s.

#1496. Roma to meet Ndicka’s entourage to discuss player’s future

Evan Ndicka has become a pillar for Gian Piero Gasperini.

In Parma, the Ivorian defender will reach 140 appearances for Roma, confirming his status as one of the most used players in recent years.

Over the last three seasons, he has logged 6,830 minutes, just 36 fewer than Mancini, who leads the rankings for outfield players with 6,866. This consistency has also been accompanied by growth in performance.

The 1999-born defender’s contract expires on June 30, 2028, meaning the Roman club will soon have to make a decision: renew or leave, keeping in mind that Ndicka holds a 20% interest in the future transfer.

The former Eintracht Frankfurt player no longer has an agent and is personally managing his future.

Evan Ndicka has played 921 minutes this season, including a headed goal against Udinese and just one yellow card.

He was precise in his tackles, making very few mistakes or lapses in form.

As Il Messaggero reports, Roma has several contract renewals lined up: in addition to De Roon and Hermoso, the Giallorossi will also begin discussions with Ndicka regarding a contract extension.

#1494. Mauricio Pochettino breaks down in TEARS as he speaks out on 'most difficult decision' to leave US for Man United after agreeing to replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford

Mauricio Pochettino broke down in tears as he began his farewell as US national team boss, and admitted that he couldn’t turn down the ‘dream’ job of Manchester United head coach.

United confirmed that Pochettino has agreed a two-and-a-half-year contract to replace Michael Carrick, and will start work on Wednesday after staying on for a double-header against Haiti.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

Mauricio Pochettino broke down in tears as he began his farewell as US national team boss

Pochettino spoke at a USMNT press conference after his move to Man United was confirmed

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

The 54-year-old Argentine revealed that United first made contact on Sunday after a 4-4 draw in Carrick’s final game left the club in the relegation zone.

United are paying US Soccer more than £10million in compensation to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts, and have allowed him to stay in charge for two more matches.

‘I never said I wanted to go back in the Premier League,’ said the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton boss, whose first game in charge of United will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

‘All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear. There was some contact. When things became bigger, they are very sensitive.

‘We were very transparent with the federation and they understand the situation. The decision between US Soccer and Man United to agree to continue for these two games will not change our commitment.

‘That decision was between the three parties but, of course if Man United agreed different terms, I need to respect that.’

Pochettino, who will oversee his side's Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti over the next week, insisted it was the 'most difficult decision' to leave the USMNT

Meanwhile, Carrick issued a statement following his sacking on Thursday after 10 months in charge.

Posting on social media, he said: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful.

‘I want to say a big thank-you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

‘That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.’

#1493. Calafiori opens to Roma return: “I’d be very happy.”

A special day for Riccardo Calafiori, honored at the Capitoline Hill by Mayor Roberto Gualtieri.

The Arsenal defender received the “Son of Rome” award for his international achievements, particularly for winning the Premier League with the Gunners. It was an opportunity to discuss his ties to the capital, as well as his past and a possible future in the Giallorossi jersey.

During the ceremony, Calafiori thanked the mayor and shared his emotion: “I feel like thanking the Mayor. I consider myself a clean-cut person, and I felt a bit emotional. I miss home, but when I return, it always feels good, and it’s a thrill.”

Calafiori then spoke about Gasperini’s Roma and the project for the new stadium in Pietralata: “We talked about the stadium project, and it’s incredible, and I can’t wait to see it finished. Speaking with the Roma guys, everyone speaks highly of Gasperini. We know how much he can develop players, and I hope he can achieve something important at the end of the season.”

Finally, the young Gunners and Italy national team defender didn’t close the door on a possible return to Roma: “I hope to win as much as possible in the coming years and achieve the best I can. I’ve always said in the distant future that we didn’t part on good terms. I don’t hold a grudge, in fact, I think it served me well. I’d be very happy.”

#1488. England's new plan of attack: Thomas Tuchel has switched style since World Cup but clunky win over Croatia showed growing pains - Spain will put it to severe test, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 16:17 EST, 13 November 2026

It was gone 11pm when Thomas Tuchel was shaking the hands of Harry Kane’s parents on the Wembley pitch while the children of England’s record appearance maker enjoyed the run of the national stadium in front of 90,000 empty seats.

This was time for Kane to fully take in the emotion of an historic night alongside his family and that Tuchel was out there too felt instructive of their relationship.

Kane and Tuchel had frank conversations last month about the World Cup fallout, on how England might be best tinkering with their selection when chasing games.

The manager respects and values his captain’s opinion on these things, recognising that he is almost completely agenda-free, as they attempt to better plot a route to silverware in readiness for the European Championship in 18 months’ time.

If there was uncertainty about identity and style when the World Cup crunch arrived, when Enzo Fernandez was pulling stupid faces and the colour drained from England faces, then players have felt that the detail on how Tuchel wants to move forward has been clear across the first two camps since America.

Thursday night was not vintage against a Croatia team they battered 7-0 a few weeks back. Tuchel and Kane both admitted that afterwards but it is noticeable that there is a defined plan on how they intend to attack in a slightly different way.

Thomas Tuchel embraces Harry Kane's wife Katie at Wembley on Thursday night

Harry Kane (centre) and Co are changing the way they attack after the World Cup

Were Tuchel to have been able to pick a first-choice back four then the win would likely have been more comfortable, Croatia benefiting from individual errors. And a lack of cutting edge inside the box hindered the hosts too.

The idea behind what they were doing appeared well thought out though and that should bring about some gentle encouragement.

The full backs, Trent Alexander-Arnold and Lewis Hall, were both consistently worked into hugely dangerous areas in the inside channels, while the make-up of Tuchel’s midfield felt very deliberate as well.

It is no coincidence that England enjoyed the highest amount of possession in the half spaces ten yards inside Croatia’s half. That is a clear directive, with both Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice drifting wider to create overloads and the full backs pushed into threatening spaces.

‘Declan understands the game like he’s almost a coach on the field and in a perfect position to manage all these things from behind,’ Tuchel said this week. To have a constant interchanging unit, he does need brains.

These are the rotations that the Three Lions didn’t engineer enough of over in the United States, with Kane dropping deep as he does and completing that wonder crossfield pass for the Morgan Rogers opener.

They are the moments that Tuchel is preaching, Jude Bellingham taking up an unusual position in order to stretch Croatia as he squared for the Chelsea forward.

What Tuchel needs now is to work on how that can be translated into making sure his very best players can affect matches more regularly inside the opponent’s box.

Jude Bellingham only touched the ball four times in Croatia's box in the 2-1 win

England manager Thomas Tuchel will speak to his players about what to do if racial abuse mars Sunday’s Nations League group decider against Spain in Madrid.

The England team have been on the wrong end of racism in Madrid before – back in 2004 – and refused to play a friendly there in 2008, insisting the fixture be moved to Seville.

In March this year, meanwhile, Spanish fans chanted anti-Muslim songs during a game with Egypt in Barcelona and the World champions have been subsequently ordered by FIFA to play their next friendly in a partially-closed stadium.

There will be a full house at Athletico Madrid’s Riyadh Air Metropolitano stadium as England try to topple Spain from the top of their group on Sunday and Tuchel said: ‘I think I hear about it [the Barcelona incident] for the first time that this happens. I think it's unacceptable.

‘In any stadium we will never accept racism.

‘I expect full support from the Spanish crowd for the Spanish team. But we will not expect anything else. And I think the referee in the games and the officials know about that.

‘I think we had a same discussion before the Serbia game [last year]. There is a protocol in place.

‘Yeah, maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Spain].’

Tuchel and the FA expect a hostile atmosphere in Madrid, especially as two Real players – Jude Bellingham and Trent Alexander-Arnold - will be in the England squad.

Last year’s Serbia game passed without incident in Belgrade and the FA are confident the same will apply this weekend.

Seven years ago in Sofia, though, captain Harry Kane almost led the England team off the field after following FIFA protocols by alerting the referee to abuse aimed at Tyrone Mings, Raheem Sterling and Marcus Rashford. The game was paused while the culprits were thrown out.

‘I still think the protocol is in place and it's important that the players know about is,’ added Tuchel.

‘And then yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. The best answers are on the pitch.’

The FIFA protocol – adopted by UEFA and the Premier League – is a four step-process that starts with a player alerting match officials and is followed by a warning to the crowd, a possible suspension of play and, if necessary, the abandonment of the game.

That Kane only touched it six times inside the 18-yard area and Bellingham on just four occasions points to a team still figuring themselves out.

That will be put to the severe test in Madrid on Sunday. England do not beat the truly elite nations; never have.

And it’ll be interesting to see whether Tuchel sticks to this sort of plan, one designed to dominate, or if he instead relies on the counter-attacking ability of a group he has viewed as a ‘Premier League team’ before now, leaning into their physicality.

If England are feeling confident enough, giving this tweaked style a go against the world champions might offer them some answers on what could be achieved when the proper silverware is on the line.

#1484. 7 Premier League managers who vanished off the face of the earth

Premier League managers are constantly in the spotlight but once they leave their role, sometimes they disappear very quickly into the background.

Plenty of Premier League managers have been on the back pages and appearing on Match of the Day one minute, only to become the answer to an obscure quiz question the next year.

Here are seven former Premier League managers who we have heard little to nothing about since they left the league.

It’s one of the more surprising names on this list considering how well he did with Huddersfield.

He took the completely unfancied Terriers up to the Premier League and even managed to keep them up, making it one of the best survival stories in the Premier League era.

The team naturally fell apart in the second season with Wagner relieved of his duties in January 2019 but his successive managerial stints have not come close to matching his time in Yorkshire.

He all but took Schalke down and then ignored interest from West Brom to sign with Young Boys. He finished second with the serial league winners before returning to England and joining Norwich.

The German reached the playoffs with the Canaries but was hammered 4-0 and new sporting director Ben Knapper handed him the sack.

That was in 2024 but Wagner has been away from the touchline ever since.

He was linked with the USMNT but these days he can be found in the boardroom of RB Leipzig as the Academy Manager.

Unsurprisingly, winning zero Premier League games and failing to score in your four attempts is likely to put an end to your future hopes of managing in the league.

Frank de Boer is one of the worst Premier League managers in history according to the stats and his career post-Selhurst Park has failed to rebuild his reputation.

He moved to Atlanta in the MLS and did actually do well, winning two cups in his first and finishing second. He got the boot in 2020 though he fell upwards to the role of Netherlands head coach.

A round of 16 loss to the Czech Republic at Euro 2020 was enough for De Boer to be sacked and his most recent job came in the UAE at Al Jazira. He could only get them to seventh though and was sacked midway through his first season.

Ever since, he has been away from the touchline except in a capacity as an analyst for Dutch TV channel ViaPlay.

Jose Mourinho’s long-time assistant went solo in 2013 as he took over Middlesbrough.

He got them up in 2016 but was always quite combustible and even started having a go at the club’s own fans for not cheering loud enough. That was the beginning of the end and he was sacked in March having fallen out with seemingly everyone at the club.

Karanka next joined Nottingham Forest but lost more games than he won and was given the sack a year later. His final appointment in England was at Birmingham, where he lost more than double the games he won.

Next he headed for Spain and Granada where he finally managed to have a positive record but not enough to keep his job and his most recent gig was four months spent as Maccabi Tel Aviv boss in 2023.

Now, he works as the technical director of development for the Spanish football federation, a role he has had since July 2025.

Long-time Fergie number two Phelan went out on his own as he took over Hull as caretaker, who had just gone up thanks to Steve Bruce. The fact that Bruce opted to resign rather than manage in the Premier League showed how big a task awaited Phelan at Hull, who at that time insisted on being called Hull City Tigers.

With a very bare squad, Phelan somehow won games against Leicester and Swansea and even picked up the Premier League Manager of the Month gong for August.

That got him the job on a permanent basis but he was sacked in January as the club slid towards relegation.

After that he went to America for a brief stint as sporting director at Central Coast Mariners but he returned to Old Trafford as coach alongside Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

When the Norwegian departed in December 2021, Phelan stayed on before three years later he followed Wayne Rooney to Plymouth Argyle to help his former player. Rooney was sacked shortly after and that ended Phelan’s time in management.

Instead, he set up his own company called Mike Phelan Coaching which provides support to grassroots clubs.

READ: Four ideal signings for Mauricio Pochettino’s Man Utd in January

The cards were stacked against Bradley when he arrived in the Premier League. He was the first American to manage in the league and was unfortunately very American.

His New Jersey accent rubbed plenty the wrong way, not least the Swansea Supporters’ Trust who owned almost a quarter of the club, and he was seen only getting the job because the club’s owners were American. His performance didn’t exactly quell that opinion.

He lost seven of his 11 games in charge before the Swansea board had to admit their mistake and sacked him the day after Boxing Day.

He left England and returned stateside where he spent 142 games in charge of LAFC. After that, he moved to Toronto but his most recent managerial stint was at Stabaek, a Norwegian side who he had managed previously.

That came to an end in 2024 and he has been out of the managerial game since. He also has gone down the punditry route and was an analyst for FOX Sports during the World Cup.

He was quite forgettable even at the time so perhaps we should not be surprised that former Swansea boss Guidolin has slipped even further from the public eye.

To be honest, we are surprised he is not Palermo manager, having been head coach there on four separate occasions.

Sacked on his 61st birthday, Guidolin left management after Swansea and is instead doing punditry and commentary work for DAZN in Italy.

Hasenhuttl’s work at Southampton (excluding the two 9-0s) felt like the start of a long career in England but not only has he been away from the country for four years, he hasn’t had a job in the last 12 months.

Following his departure from the Saints, he joined Bundesliga strugglers Wolfsburg, saving them from relegation.

He kept them clear of relegation troubles for the beginning of his first full campaign in charge but eight matches without a win, the last of which was a 4-0 defeat to Borussia Dortmund, spooked the board and he was sacked.

As for what he has been doing since, your guess is as good as ours. Not much has been heard of Hasenhuttl since his Wolfsburg departure. It would seem likely that at 59, he still fancies working in management but he has been waiting a while now.

#1483. Patrick Dorgu sent home from Denmark duty after failing fitness tests - just hours after joining up with team-mates - in early blow for new Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino

Published: 17:03 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 13 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino already has a fresh injury headache at Manchester United - and he's not even through the door yet.

Patrick Dorgu has been sent home from Denmark duty having failed a series of physical tests.

The full-back missed four Premier League matches in October due to a hamstring injury but came on to provide an assist and score the equaliser in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday.

Now he re-joins an injury list which includes Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw, Carlos Baleba, and potentially Harry Maguire, with Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko ruled out longer-term.

Denmark's team doctor Martin Boesen said: 'We have carried out a series of tests on Dorgu, and he has not performed well enough to be ready to play in the two matches.

'He needs further recovery time after his injury, so we are sending him home for additional rehabilitation.'

Patrick Dorgu has been sent home fromDenmark duty after failing a series of fitness tests

It is potentially another thing for incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino to worry about

Dorgu, 22, will miss matches against Portugal and Norway in the Nations League.

Pochettino will hope Dorgu makes a quick recovery as he seeks to get Manchester United back on track.

United, who sit 18th in the Premier League, agreed to pay more than £10million to prise Pochettino and his staff away from the United States national team.

Pochettino has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Michael Carrick and will get down to business after his final matches in charge of the USA against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

The former Southampton, Tottenham, and Chelsea boss broke down in tears as he began his farewell and admitted that he couldn’t turn down the ‘dream’ job of Manchester United head coach.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

The 54-year-old Argentine revealed that United first made contact on Sunday after the 4-4 draw in Carrick’s final game left the club in the relegation zone.

‘I never said I wanted to go back in the Premier League,’ said Pochettino, whose first game in charge of United will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

‘All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear. There was some contact. When things became bigger, they are very sensitive.

‘We were very transparent with the federation and they understand the situation. The decision between US Soccer and Man United to agree to continue for these two games will not change our commitment.

‘That decision was between the three parties but, of course if Man United agreed different terms, I need to respect that.’
