#1355. 'Am I supposed to answer that?': Erling Haaland breaks silence and distances himself from Man City cheating verdict as star striker insists 'I don't really know much... I was playing for Bryne Under 9s'

Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026

Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.

Man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Haaland was quizzed about the club's situation by Norwegian broadcaster TV2, after scoring in the national team's 3-1 victory over Wales on Saturday.

The Man City star's initial answer lasted for two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges.

Erling Haaland insisted it was difficult for him to answer a question about Man City's guilty verdict, with the club appealing against the decision of an independent commission. Source: TV2Sport

Haaland stressed he remains happy at the club after being asked about his future given the potential ramificiations if Man City fail with their appeal to overturn the verdict.

'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland began.

'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle…

'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'

Haaland continued by listing fellow Norwegians who had been at Man City at the time, joking that they may be in a better place to offer insight.

'There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think,' Haaland said.

'Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can't remember.

The forward distanced himself from the case as he listed team he played from 2009-18, the time covered by the charges. Pictured: Haaland in action for Molde in 2018

'But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

'A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there.'

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Haaland, who has won eight major honours at the club including the Treble in 2023, was asked about whether the case has affected his thoughts on his Man City future.

'I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,' Haaland responded.

'I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

'I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we're top of our group in Europe.

'Things aren't going so well for City in the league, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can't focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.'

Man City have won twice and lost three times in the Premier League since the independent commission verdict was announced in September.

Enzo Maresca's side have slipped to six points behind reigning champions Arsenal following their drop off in form.

#1354. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

🗣️ Commitment. Resilience. Teamwork. Michael's powerful message in full 👇 https://t.co/vWwJt1fW47

This was partly Carrick reasserting his own authority after a couple of weeks in which two senior players – defender Lisandro Martínez and captain Bruno Fernandes – decided to go public with their grievances and the team delivered a performance in the 4-1 hammering by Como that was up there with the very worst.

But a stony-faced Carrick was also sending a message to his squad to quit their public sniping and start pulling together for a wider cause. Moreover, to put the club and the team before yourself and your individual needs and complaints.

It was interesting that he used the word “entitlement”. His predecessor, Ruben Amorim, had uttered that same word to attack what he felt was an “entitlement culture” at the club and Carrick has evidently come to a similar conclusion.

"I think it's the feeling of entitlement that we have in our club" Ruben Amorim says some of the players at Manchester United may need a bit of a reality check 🎙️ https://t.co/PiJWML3TeH

In truth, so many of the post-Ferguson managers have spoken in similar ways – certainly Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Jose Mourinho and Ralf Rangnick.

Listening to Carrick repeatedly talking about the need for humility, hard work, pride, sacrifice and resilience was a reminder of how the values that were once taken for granted at this football club have steadily been eroded.

Wayne Rooney said this week that United’s players were “selfish” and “babies”. Many top players over the years have been selfish but it helped drive them and, in turn, their team to great heights, but the same cannot be said about the current bunch.

Carrick spoke about trying to rediscover something that is “lost” at the moment. Whether they can is a big if. Opponents aside, the only winners at the moment from United’s latest crisis are Amazon.

It feels at times as if it can be a long way away but it doesn’t take too much to flip the other way and we’re more than capable of doing that, I totally believe that.

We will. We’ll win football matches and we’ve got a very tough one on Sunday [against Bournemouth].

Very, very good team that we’re playing again and I’m not suggesting that becomes an easy game because it doesn’t. We’ve got to respect the game, respect what it takes to win.

We’ve spoken. There are always conversations going on. It’s pretty obvious how we’re all feeling. A reaction, a reaction from me.

The responsibility for me in this position is to lead. It is my responsibility, whatever goes on the pitch and what we look like, what we feel like.

Carrick had clearly thought hard about how he was going to tackle that today and what message he wanted to get across. The long and short of it was that the United manager was issuing a call to arms to his players to pull their finger out, respect the badge and start showing the kind of values of humility and hard work that the club is founded on. By name checking the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Matt Busby he was speaking about the people who exemplified the values United are all about

The foundations of this football club and values have been etched down for many years.

I totally understand and I get every single one of them. It comes down to being humble, to hard work and being really proud to live up to those values.

There is a resilience about this football club that has been shown for a long, long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, sustaining success, there is a resilience to this football club that runs very, very deep.

No definitive answer from Carrick, who says he wants to do what is best for the football club.

There ends the broadcast section of the press conference after about 15 minutes.

Definitely a change in communication strategy from Carrick, speaking from the heart rather than waiting for questions.

My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, represents the supporters and they can be proud of it with the identity that we show.

We have gone away from that just recently in certain games, which I’m fully aware of and definitely doing something about.

I think it’s important we all recognise that. I certainly recognise it. Our supporters of are the utmost importance to me and this football club.

For them to feel like they felt for five months at the start of the year and have that about us, that connection and that real vigour, intensity and enjoyment and passion is something we need to get back to.

Carrick says the dressing room is “not divided” but says it’s pretty clear the squad and everyone have to pull together and stop speaking out like has happened in public in response to questions about Martinez and Fernandes’ outbursts.

Principles are so important. We can win games, lose games, hopefully not but it can happen.

It’s how you do it and what it feels like is important for me. That the spirit and togetherness is there. It will be there. I’m working on solutions to move us forward.

I haven’t invented anything new, it’s the make-up of any good football team. You have to earn the right to be better than your opponent, that’s not changed and it never changes.

He says loads of conversations have been going on. He says it’s his responsibility “to lead” and that “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and keep everyone else dry.”

Carrick adds on the Fernandes burglary. “It’s an awful thing to go through and we’re doing a lot of things to support him and his family.”

It was never about Ryan Giggs, it was never about Ryan Giggs, it was about Manchester United.

Wayne Rooney is top goalscorer of this football club. His biggest thing was playing for the team, sacrificing for the team and what was good for Manchester United.

Sir Alex Ferguson is the best manager of all-time. The greatest, for me. And working for him, his main priority was Manchester United.

Sir Matt [Busby] and Sir Bobby [Charlton], their resilience was beyond belief what they showed and how they rebuilt this football club. It was based on being humble, having humility and hard work. We can never lose that and I won’t let us lose that.

We’ve lost our way if I’m totally honest but we’ll get back what it takes.

Carrick has come in, trailed by the Amazon cameras, sat down and made an address for five minutes before taking any questions. He acknowledges it’s not been good enough or what the club expects and that it’s got to get better. He’s talking about rebuilding this club based on humility, values and hard work and won’t let that go and that it inspires him going forward. “Yeah we’re in a moment where it’s not going well but we need to show exactly what it means and respect what it means to be here and what it takes to win,” he said. “You’re not entitled to win. It takes hard work.”

I think it’s important... recently we haven’t had a good time I think that’s obvious, I totally accept that.

We had five months of relative success and I was happy with many things I was seeing.

We haven’t done well enough recently. Wednesday was a bad night for a lot of reasons, it really hurt a lot, it hurt me to see how the game panned out.

As I said after the game, it was unacceptable.

Hopefully he will be in position by half-past, but it is not unlike managers to keep everyone waiting.

Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

Just look at the performance of Ineos’s other prize assets this season: Lausanne-Sport lie 12th in the 12-team Swiss top flight after one win in 10, and Nice are a distant 13th in Ligue 1, having burnt through eight different managers during the petrochemical giant’s seven years in charge.

As James Ducker and Sam Dean explore in this piece, a succession of Manchester United managers have admonished their team for a lack of industry and athleticism. A number of factors may be to blame: recruitment errors, paralysing pressure and a bad dressing-room culture among them. It is time to get back to basics.

Michael Carrick is not one of the Premier League’s more loquacious managers but supporters will be interested in what he has to say at his pre-Bournemouth press conference this afternoon.

The Manchester United manager is under severe pressure after a run of no wins in seven games across all competitions, and senior players are talking out of school in post-game interviews.

Just when it appeared a line had been drawn under Lisandro Martinez taking on technical director Jason Wilcox, Bruno Fernandes reached for a petrol can and poured more fuel on the flames.

Speaking after the dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes called out Carrick and his coaching staff for their tactical approach, specifically a reluctance to press opponents aggressively in a man-to-man fashion.

Carrick, by his own very measured standards, delivered a pointed response.

“We actually were half-pressed man to man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that,” he said. “And there’s a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

Their opponents on Sunday are Bournemouth, who after a lean run of results under Marco Rose have just dispatched Sunderland for their first league victory of the season, and the mighty AC Milan in the Europa League.

Things do not get easier for United, who go to Stamford Bridge next weekend before a home game against Aston Villa before the November international break.

Telegraph Sport reported on Thursday that former Bayern Munich and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann features prominently and is understood to want the job – as does Antonio Conte. United are also tracking Fabian Hurzeler while there is interest in Eddie Howe.

United are currently 13th in the table with seven points from seven games.

Manchester United and Manchester City have reportedly entered the race to sign Bayern Munich youngster Leonard Prescott, with Arsenal also among the Premier League clubs interested in securing his signature.

The 17-year-old goalkeeper is attracting considerable attention across Europe, having developed a reputation as one of German football’s most exciting young prospects.

According to a TEAMtalk report, both Manchester clubs have contacted Prescott’s representatives as they explore the possibility of bringing him to England.

Arsenal have been monitoring his situation for some time, while Chelsea, Tottenham and Juventus have also expressed an interest in the highly-rated teenager.

Prescott’s future at the Allianz Arena has grown increasingly uncertain, with contract extension talks failing to progress as Bayern would have hoped. His current agreement expires next summer, potentially allowing interested clubs to secure his services without paying a transfer fee.

The biggest concern for the young goalkeeper is his pathway into Bayern’s senior team. Manuel Neuer is expected to retire at the end of the season, but the German champions are already preparing Jonas Urbig to become their first-choice goalkeeper.

Bayern are also considering experienced alternatives, meaning Prescott could find himself further down the pecking order rather than receiving opportunities to establish himself.

That situation could make a departure increasingly attractive, particularly with several clubs prepared to offer him a more convincing development plan.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

However, a significant obstacle remains for Manchester United, Manchester City and Arsenal. Prescott will not celebrate his 18th birthday until September 2027, meaning a move to England could be delayed until 2028 under the relevant transfer regulations.

This gives Bayern an opportunity to persuade the youngster to reconsider his position and commit his long-term future to the club.

Nevertheless, the growing interest from the Premier League could make negotiations increasingly difficult for the Bundesliga giants.

Manchester United and Manchester City have the financial resources and infrastructure to compete for promising young talents, while Arsenal could offer Prescott an attractive route towards senior football.

Much will depend on the guarantees each club can provide regarding his development and first-team opportunities.

Bayern Munich are reportedly stepping up their efforts to sign Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha, but the Premier League giants remain determined to keep hold of the highly-rated winger despite growing interest from Germany.

The 18-year-old has emerged as one of the most exciting young prospects in English football, attracting attention from several European heavyweights following his impressive development at Anfield.

According to a TEAMtalk report, Bayern have recently contacted Ngumoha’s representatives to explore bringing him to the Allianz Arena.

The Bundesliga champions are keen to strengthen their attacking options and have identified the Liverpool youngster as a potential addition. However, convincing the Merseyside club to sanction his departure will be extremely difficult.

Liverpool have no intention of letting the teenager leave during the January transfer window, viewing him as an important part of their long-term project.

Ngumoha has already made 44 appearances for the senior side, contributing two goals and three assists. His pace, dribbling ability and confidence in one-on-one situations have made him an exciting prospect for the future.

The Reds are particularly encouraged by his development and believe he has the potential to become one of Europe’s leading attacking talents.

#1351. 'Managers now are b****y boring!': NEIL WARNOCK on the lack of characters in football, his friendship with Pep Guardiola, why he is open to managing again post-Christmas - and how he almost became a chiropodist!

Published: 19:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 16 November 2026

Spending time in the company of Neil Warnock is always an education, be it witnessing one of his legendary foul-mouthed touchline rants or perched at one of his stage shows at grand venues like London Palladium.

On this occasion, Daily Mail Sport is perched in an east London bar watching on as one of English football's national treasures is posing for some modelling. Yes, you read that right, Mr Warnock is here to launch his own pair of socks with a tipple of Famous Grouse whisky in hand.

The complements on Warnock's 77-year-old feet are soon over, though, and we can get on to talking about a life in football that started six decades ago as a winger for Chesterfield and has traversed 10 clubs as a player, 17 as a manager and more than 2,000 games in the dugout.

So where to start? Maybe his reflections on nearly five decades in management – and how the whole conversation about feet is not too out of place…

'You don't realise how long it has been really, I started off just a team of ragamuffins as I call them,' he says in his iconic Yorkshire accent. 'They used to train on the green where I had digs in Hartlepool and asked me to coach them.

'I remember we scored from a set-piece we worked on, I was running up and down the touchline high-fiving everyone. I got the bug. I knew I could never get to the top as a player, I was quick but I was brainless.

Daily Mail Sport caught up with Neil Warnock to discuss his six decades in football

After representing 10 different clubs as a player, Warnock became one of the most compelling managers in the game

'I could've been a chiropodist if not in football. That could be on a quiz, couldn't it? I had bad feet at Scunthorpe, I used to get massive blisters so the physio there started getting me to do some of the players' feet.

'I enjoyed doing ingrown toenails and things like that! So I thought why not? Then I had a practice in Sheffield. I had to make a decision when we won the league at Scarborough whether to go full-time or pack it in. I thought, "Oh, go on then, let's give it a little go".

'It's not worked out badly, really, has it?

'People come up to me every day and say, "You're a legend, you". And I say, "Oh, thank you very much". Then they tell me what club they support, I have had so many haven't I? Last week I went out for a minute and had four selfies. They all appreciate what I did for their club.

'There aren't as many characters in the game now, you wouldn't get upset with managers now like in my day because now they are that b****y boring! Some of them barely speak.

'They won't get the rapport we had. I managed at a good time. The way I managed, I needed that humour. I needed the lads to enjoy it. I signed a lot of players that many managers wouldn't touch with a barge pole, are you with me? They ended up getting me promotions.'

The aforementioned humour brings us on to a private conversation he had with the great Pep Guardiola, one of the millions of anecdotes up Warnock's sleeve but one that he has not told until now.

'I went to a training session and he asked me to say a few words,' explains Warnock. 'I said, "Well lads I bet you're glad I'm not your manager because we'd be kicking balls from there to there, chasing it, heading it, practicing our tackles"... everyone laughed.

Warnock views Pep Guardiola as the best manager of his lifetime, while the Spaniard praised the veteran's humour after once addressing his Man City squad at a training session

Warnock has led teams to promotions on eight occasions over the course of his career

'After the session we had a coffee and Pep said to me, "Neil, that was amazing, you know when you talked to the players? I understood why you had so many promotions".

'He started counting and said, "What we have is all these staff… computers, details, nutritionist, all these staff, but you know what we don't have? Humour". He noticed why my lads had done well in my teams, just in that meeting. It was good, that. He is amazing.

'Pep is the best manager of my lifetime. They say he had all the best players but it is not easy managing them. Pep did things with players and now there are non-league teams trying to play like Manchester City!'

Warnock is now doing stage tours - Guardiola attended one last season - and had a tear in his eye when he stepped out at London Palladium given he used to watch shows there with his mother, who was in a wheelchair, on the TV as a child.

So what is Warnock up to these days? His current role is advisor at Torquay United but last management job was at Aberdeen two years ago… so is he out of the rat race for good this time?

'No, not really, no,' he says. 'I only work from February to April! So the phone will be on after Christmas. You never know, do ya? There will be someone thinking "why don't we get that Warnock in?".

'I've retired 40 times! Every time I have said it, I have meant it. But it's that dressing room camaraderie. There's something about football, when I look at some of the managers now… they just don't excite me.

'I remember Ruben Amorim (breaks down laughing). He's got his computer out on the bench! I remember watching and thinking, "I'm sorry, son, you need more than a computer to help you tonight!".

Warnock is currently doing stage tours, with Guardiola among the attendees last season

Warnock's current role is advisor at Torquay United and briefly served as interim manager last season, with the 77-year-old admitting he had not completely ruled out a return to the dugout

'And likewise, I see them making notes on the bench, oh my god. I think "what are you doing, your shopping list for Tescos?".

'I do enjoy walking and I enjoy photography, believe it or not. I go up the river with my phone, there's so many lovely things to see.

'I've got an electric bike and I sometimes do about 25 miles. I was thinking of doing a cycle of all my clubs but that would take me five years! They go at about 30mph down the hills, you've got to be careful, you wouldn't want to come off them.'

He is also enjoying fishing, being with the family and playing golf with his son, a PGA rising star William - though Warnock Sr insists he often embarrasses himself playing off 'the ladies' tee'.

The thing that makes Warnock most proud is the four promotions at Wembley but also the togetherness he fostered in his many teams.

He tells us: 'What I like about the teams I had, they all have reunions. You look at the tele now, someone will score a goal and kiss the badge… they won't have a reunion.

'When I go to these reunions, I see all my lads and how I blended that dressing room together and I look at the comradeship they still have now, they are the same as they were just a lot older.

'This year, my Scarborough team are having a 40-year celebration and the lads have invited me. I said there's no way I'm going out with that lot after the do because they can drink, let me tell you!'

* The Famous Grouse has teamed up with Happy Socks to launch an exclusive limited-edition collection, available at Tesco stores across the UK. Shoppers can pick up a free pair of colourful, collectable socks with selected 70cl bottles of The Famous Grouse whisky, priced from £18.50. Available in-store only, while stocks last.

Tottenham Hotspur have received a boost on Pedro Porro’s future, with Fabrizio Romano dismissing speculation that the defender could join Barcelona in the January transfer window.

The Spanish international has attracted considerable attention at home, with Barcelona reportedly keen to bring him back to La Liga after his impressive Premier League performances.

According to a TEAMtalk report, Romano has clarified that Tottenham and Barcelona are not currently in negotiations over a potential January transfer.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, the transfer expert said Spurs are satisfied with the 27-year-old and have no intention of letting him leave midway through the campaign.

Romano also pointed out that Porro recently committed his future to the north London outfit by signing a new contract, with the agreement keeping him at the club until 2031.

Romano revealed on YouTube: “Tottenham absolutely don’t consider an exit of Pedro Porro in January. Tottenham are very happy with Pedro Porro; there is no tension between Pedro Porro and Tottenham.

“Pedro Porro, in January, is expected to stay. Nothing ongoing with Barcelona for the January transfer window.

“Then, summer is another story. We will see, it’s still far away, we are in November.

“But I wanted to clarify, there are no active negotiations for Pedro Porro, from Tottenham to Barcelona. So the situation is completely quiet.

“He’s an important player for De Zerbi, he’s an important player for Spurs.

“His new contract was signed five months ago, so everyone [is] happy to continue together. Then, we will see again in the summer.”

The latest development is encouraging for Tottenham, given the defender’s importance to their attacking and defensive structure.

Porro has established himself as one of the most influential full-backs in the Premier League, combining his defensive responsibilities with excellent attacking contributions.

Barcelona’s interest is understandable, given their need to strengthen their defensive options, but Tottenham will be reluctant to lose such an important player.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Meanwhile, a summer departure has not been ruled out, with Romano suggesting the situation could change once the current campaign concludes.

For now, however, Tottenham can remain confident about retaining their defensive asset, and Barcelona will have to wait before considering whether to pursue a deal.

Porro’s immediate future appears to be in North London, although speculation surrounding a potential return to Spain could gather momentum again next summer.

#1348. ‘Tactical genius’ Emery outsmarts Maresca as City crash to first league defeat

Enzo Maresca’s flawless start to the Premier League with Manchester City is over after another masterclass from Unai Emery.

Matches at Villa Park were a notoriously chastening experience for Pep Guardiola and it was the same old story for Maresca as City have now lost on their last four visits here.

On his fourth anniversary in charge of Villa, there was more tactical brilliance from Emery, who also did the double over Guardiola last season. It was Emery’s £65m record signing Nicolas Jackson who again underlined how some managers can get the best out of certain players.

Jackson had been a target for Emery ever since the Basque’s appointment and now has seven goals in claret and blue. It will have been an especially sweet moment for the Senegal forward, for it was Maresca who allowed him to join Bayern Munich on loan while he was in charge at Chelsea.

City’s run of seven league wins in a row always looked in danger here against a vibrant and energetic Villa. Maresca will also reflect on two poor goals conceded after errors from Marc Guéhi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Guéhi endured a particularly difficult afternoon and was at fault for Jackson’s stunning first goal. The centre-back has struggled in recent weeks with a bad mistake in England’s defeat by Spain and he was exposed for both Ipswich goals last week. He was replaced at half-time after a booking for a foul on the excellent Jackson.

What a strike from Nicolas Jackson to beat Gianluigi Donnarumma 😲 Villa Park erupts 🔊 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/zkuDVMevKF

Maresca said: “I’m not worried about Marc at all, he is playing every game since the season started for us and the national team so it’s not easy. He is ok, it [taking him off] was just a technical decision and like in all games managers make changes. He was on a yellow card and sometimes one yellow card can be dangerous.”

When asked if the goals were avoidable, Maresca said: “Absolutely, both. Sometimes you have to be a bit more lucky because we only conceded those two chances. We will try again to win at Villa next season. I don’t think we deserved to lose but we learn from that and move on. You can always learn something. For sure there are things we can do better today.”

While much of the focus will be on City’s 100 per cent start to the league coming to an end, Emery got everything right here. From his team selection to his set-up and substitutions, he outsmarted Maresca on many levels. After the game, Villa defender Matty Cash described his manager as “a tactical genius”.

It was four years ago to the day that Emery grabbed this famous club by the shirt and collar and gave them an almighty shake. After a summer of much instability including many player sales, he appears to have already struck a formula with his newly assembled team.

There were a number of fine individual performances from many of the summer arrivals, such as Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi.

Emery said: “We were very motivated and Manchester City is the best team in the world so this is the level. This year we started so poorly and we needed time to understand how we improve. The players showed the capacity to retrieve the level we’ve had over the last few years.

“Nicolas is more mature and very demanding of himself to improve. Earlier this season he was shooting over the crossbar but he is now finding the corners. There is still work to do and 11 points is not enough but we are feeling better.”

Villa were fierce from the start and ahead after six minutes. Guéhi’s mistake was punished by John McGinn, with the ball dropping to Jackson who crashed a shot into the roof of the net.

He writes: “With Pep Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp having departed the Premier League, there can now be little doubt that Unai Emery is the best manager in England’s top division. And by some distance.

“Saturday will mark four years since Villa unveiled Emery as their head coach and few could have predicted the success that has followed. He has proved an inspired appointment who has continually embarrassed the “Big Six” clubs.

“On every level, he has delivered: points per game, net spend, a distinguishable style of play, improving individual players, over-performance in the league and European competition.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

Manchester United are reportedly keen on a potential January move for Barcelona defender Alejandro Balde, with super-agent Jorge Mendes expected to meet the player in Spain today.

The Reds are believed to be satisfied with their current options in most positions and do not see any area of the squad as urgently needing reinforcement. However, the club remain attentive to opportunities that could help them secure long-term targets earlier than initially anticipated.

#1345. England's evolution: James Trafford and two other stars chisel their names into the XI, Thomas Tuchel learning from Argentina and Jude Bellingham playing like a captain!

Published: 02:32 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:25 EST, 16 November 2026

England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.

After Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored to establish a three-goal lead, the visitors had to cling on after Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts scored twice in the final half hour.

The victory means Thomas Tuchel's side top their Nations League group and it provided a strong riposte to criticism of the manager following the World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was at the Metropolitano Stadium, and here are his FIVE big take-aways…

It would not have mattered had England conceded a late equaliser. To draw comparison with Argentina in the final half hour is unfair and inaccurate. The World Cup semi-final was 11v11 and so, when we draw conclusions from this game, let us do so on the same terms.

Thomas Tuchel was delighted with his England players as they won 3-2 away in Spain

And what did England do at 11v11 with a 1-0 lead? They attacked. And attacked again. This was a major change (and improvement) and is the reason for such encouragement. They have learnt from a mistake, as much as Tuchel will be loathe to admit.

Mexico would be a fairer parallel, but that was against opposition far inferior to Spain. At 11v10, we could not expect England to stay on the front foot here, as they were until the point of Jarell Quansah's needless mistake and Elliot Anderson's subsequent red card.

And that is cause for great optimism - because this game was not in the balance in any way when the teams were at equal number.

For me, and I don't think this is even close, this was the best performance of Tuchel's reign.

Do England suddenly have a pair of full backs?! After years of trawling and trialling, here in the most testing of surrounds, Ben White and Lewis Hall inked their names into Tuchel's XI.

We can forgive the concession of two goals when down to 10 men - because with 11, Spain barely looked like getting a shot on target. In fact, they didn't.

Much of that was down to the solidity of the full backs. Then, with backs to the wall, the pair became bricks in the resistance. One White block late on was heroic.

Before that, Hall's best work was not in containing Lamine Yamal, but in emulating him. His dribbles were daring and unnerved Spain, who thought they would spend the game in England's half and with the ball. They did neither early on and Hall was central to that.

White's goal had shades of Carlos Alberto on the overlap, and his England redemption arc felt like it reached completion here. Let him now move on now, for England need him.

No more boos, please, only cheers for White (and Hall).

It's time to stop the boos for Ben White after he starred with Lewis Hall at full back

Ezri Konsa is England's best defender. Build the backline around him.

Tuchel said on the eve of the game that he thought Konsa had grown for the move to Arsenal, and this was proof.

Boy do England need a mature, reliable presence at the heart of their defence. Konsa showed here why he can be that man. He scored a fine goal, which is always a sign of a defender ready to take wider responsibility, but it was his cool interceptions and desperate blocks at the other end that were most reassuring.

What Konsa has to do now is build on this - and a man-of-the-match performance at the home of the world champions is a pretty lofty and solid foundation from which to do so.

Tuchel will, and should, be giving serious thought to keeping James Trafford in England's goal for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Jordan Pickford has done nothing wrong. And yet, it feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and here was his justification.

Trafford can be a little erratic and immature. What better way to grow, emotionally, than with a series of saves to preserve an historic win. He will feel like a different player, and person, to the one who started this game. Like White and Hall, this felt like a coming-of-age night in an England jersey.

Trafford has all the tools. He might just have used them to chisel his name into that team-sheet.

Goalkeeper feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and James Trafford starred

Spain's fans are left shocked as Ezri Konsa hails the brilliant Trafford in emphatic fashion

No goals, but England would not have won this game without Bellingham. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his brilliance.

Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too.

His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. Of all the positives from this win, it is hard to look past Bellingham as the biggest reason for England being able to challenge Spain at the top of the world rankings.

Jude Bellingham played like a captain, dropping into midfield when down to 10 men

He won the corner for the second goal and created the third. He then dropped into midfield when down to 10 and played like a captain.

That is what England need - Bellingham the leader, not Bellingham the individual. He has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. They don't come much bigger than what England achieved here.

#1344. New CRISPR therapy is poised to gain first FDA approval to alter genes inside the body

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Heidi Ledford reports for Nature from Seattle, Washington.

The Cas9 protein (blue; artist’s illustration) together with RNA and DNA (orange). A new therapy uses the CRISPR–Cas9 gene-editing system to treat a rare genetic disorder called hereditary angioedema.Credit: Alfred Pasieka/SPL

A pioneering therapy that edits genes inside a recipient’s body continues to be effective four years after treatment, according to data released by its developer, Intellia Therapeutics.

The therapy, named lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z), was designed to treat one form of a genetic condition that can cause episodes of painful and potentially dangerous swelling in the throat and other parts of the body. Lonvo-z deploys the CRISPR–Cas9 gene-editing system to disable the gene that produces prekallikrein, a protein made in the liver that promotes blood-vessel leakage.

Bigger than CRISPR? A guide to the latest genome editors

Bigger than CRISPR? A guide to the latest genome editors

Intellia, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has applied for approval of lonvo-z by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), which is expected to issue a decision by 10 March. If approved, the therapy will become the world’s first CRISPR medicine to be delivered directly inside the body, or in vivo, John Leonard, Intellia’s chief executive, told investors on 12 November. Currently, the only CRISPR therapy approved by the FDA is performed on cells that have been removed from the body and are subsequently re-infused.

For people with the condition, a type of hereditary angioedema, the gene-editing approach could offer relief from a lifetime of juggling medications to prevent and treat swelling attacks, says Jonathan Bernstein, a hereditary-angioedema specialist at the University of Cincinnati in Ohio and an investigator on a lonvo-z trial. “It’s very reassuring,” he says of the four-year data. “That’s what you’re supposed to see.”

The only approved CRISPR therapy is Casgevy, a treatment for two genetic blood disorders, sickle-cell disease and β-thalassaemia. To create a dose of Casgevy, physicians first remove blood stem cells from the recipient, then send the cells off for gene editing before infusing them back into the recipient.

The therapy must be made anew for each person, adding time, cost and complexity. The recipient also has to undergo harsh chemotherapy treatment to make room for the edited cells.

CRISPR makes enhanced cancer-fighting immune cells inside mice

CRISPR makes enhanced cancer-fighting immune cells inside mice

In vivo gene-editing approaches aim to sidestep these concerns by editing genes directly in the body. Lonvo-z, for example, consists of fatty particles that encase mRNA encoding CRISPR–Cas9 components. The particles are infused into the blood and taken up by the liver, where prekallikrein is produced. The procedure takes one day.

In vivo gene editing can introduce other safety concerns, however. The therapy affords no opportunity to screen out cells with unwanted edits at other locations in the genome. Recipients might also have harmful immune responses to the treatment.

Last year, the FDA placed a clinical hold on two of Intellia’s in vivo trials for a different disorder. The agency did so after a participant with additional health conditions developed signs of liver damage and died after receiving a CRISPR treatment. The FDA lifted the hold this year after extra safety measures were added.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03705-9

#1343. Maignan and Milan receive positive verdict after France injury scare

Tests Mike Maignan underwent this morning ruled out a serious injury for the Milan keeper, who is expected to be available against Frosinone on Sunday.

Milan have received positive news from their goalkeeper, Maignan, who was forced to be subbed off during his latest game with the French national team.

Sky Sport Italia and MilanNews are among the Italian sources reporting that exams of the experienced goalkeeper have ruled out a lesion, meaning the Milan star is expected to be available for the upcoming Serie A match against Frosinone.

Today’s results confirm the outcome of medical tests already undergone in France, which highlighted no serious injury for the 31-year-old.

Maignan has conceded 16 goals in 14 appearances for Milan across all competitions this season, keeping four clean sheets.

The France international played the full game against the Italy national team on Friday, but was subbed off at half-time in his national team’s 2-1 victory over Turkiye on Sunday.

Milan sit fourth in the Serie A table with 24 points from 11 games and four wins in their last five league matches.

Lorenzo Bettoni is the Editor of Football Italia.

Leicester City are facing a potentially significant squad overhaul next summer, with nine players expected to leave the club as several contract decisions approach at the King Power Stadium.

The Foxes are focused on securing promotion from League One on the first attempt, but the club’s hierarchy will also need to consider long-term squad planning as the season draws to a close.

According to a report from Leicester Mercury, academy graduate Sammy Braybrooke is among those whose future requires attention, with his current contract due to expire next summer.

The 22-year-old midfielder has become an important member of Russell Martin’s side this season, and Leicester will be keen to avoid losing a promising homegrown talent without receiving a transfer fee.

Braybrooke is not the only academy graduate approaching the end of his current agreement. Goalkeeper Jakub Stolarczyk and defender Ben Nelson are also expected to see their contracts expire next summer, although their respective long-term knee injuries could complicate decisions over their futures.

Meanwhile, Bobby De Cordova-Reid and goalkeeper David Cornell are also approaching the end of their Leicester contracts. The former has registered nine goals in 80 appearances since arriving from Fulham in 2024, but an extension appears unlikely.

The club will additionally need to assess the futures of several loan players, with Tammy Watson, Kamari Doyle, Harry Howell and Christian McFarlane expected to return to their parent clubs when their temporary arrangements conclude.

Further contractual matters remain to be addressed in 2028, with John Lundstram, Will Alves, Harry Souttar, Bade Aluko and Alex McCarthy among those whose agreements are nearing their end.

Leicester’s immediate priority remains promotion, but the club cannot afford to overlook its long-term planning. Finding an agreement with Braybrooke could be particularly important as they look to retain emerging talent.
